Subject: Medico activation runway — on-prem/VPC info & next steps

Hi Samir —

Great to have MedicoHealth progressing to on-prem/VPC activation. To keep the first-week kickoff tight, can you send the items below by EOD tomorrow? I’ve put the initial checklist inline so engineering can triage immediately.

Quick ask list (minimum viable set):
- VPC CIDR(s) and target account IDs (we need exact blocks to validate routing overlap)
- BGP ASN if you plan to use dynamic peering (or confirmation that static routes are preferred)
- Peering model: Direct Connect / Cloud Interconnect / IPsec VPN (and expected cutover practice)
- Public egress IPs (if you need allowlist) and expected outbound ranges for health checks
- KMS provider details (ARN or key ID) + rotation policy summary
- SOC2 / logging evidence (if available) or a timeline for providing it
- Expected RPS and percentiles for 95/99 latency with sample request sizes
- Preferred weekly maintenance window (timezone) for any kernel/network-level changes

Attachments: I’ve attached our lightweight preflight template — please fill VPC table + attach your infra diagram if handy.

Next steps: once we have these, Ben will run a network acceptance checklist and Kimberly will validate KMS/compliance items. I’ll schedule a 45-min kickoff to walk through the diagram and confirm peering. Suggested time slots tomorrow afternoon (PDT) — which works for you?

Thanks —
Jordan Blake

Quick answers below and I attached our infra diagram + VPC CIDR sheet. High level: we plan to use a managed colocation + single VPC per environment (prod/stage).

- VPC CIDRs: prod 10.10.0.0/16, stage 10.11.0.0/16 (see attached medico_vpc_cidr.xlsx)
- BGP ASN: 64512 (we will do BGP peering via our colo partner)
- Peering: Colocation Direct Connect to Redwood edge; primary with active-active BGP, fallback over IPsec VPN
- Public egress: currently NATed through our egress gateway; range when assigned by colo will be sent tomorrow (we have a small static pool)
- KMS: AWS KMS customer-managed key (arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01) — rotation every 90 days
- SOC2: we have a current SOC2 Type II report — I can upload redacted copy (legal needs to scrub first). Timeline: 48–72 hours for sanitized version
- Traffic profile: peak 220 RPS, typical payload ~1.1KB, 95th latency target <200ms to Redwood endpoint (we’ll send sample traffic later)
- Maintenance: Tuesdays 02:00–04:00 UTC preferred

I attached: medico_infra_diagram.pdf, medico_vpc_cidr.xlsx.

Let me know which time slot tomorrow works for the kickoff (I’m in EST).

Subject: Re: Medico activation runway — on-prem/VPC info & next steps

Thanks Samir — good detail, appreciated. A few follow-ups from the network/ops side so we can validate before the kickoff:

1) BGP details
- Can you share the exact neighbor IPs you intend to use for the BGP sessions and the expected AS path prep rules (if any)?

2) MTU and fragmentation
- Please confirm MTU on colo fabric (we have seen 9000 in some colo setups). If jumbo frames are used we’ll validate MTU consistency end-to-end.

3) Health-check and session ports
- Ports we’ll need open: 443 (HTTPS), 5233 (Redwood control plane, example), 22 (bastion for debug), 123 (NTP), 25 (if mail callbacks), and ephemeral for outbound connections.
- We recommend a dedicated bastion host with restricted CIDR for our support engineers (we can provide a short-lived cert-based jump if needed).

4) IP allowlist process
- Once public egress ranges are finalized, we’ll provide a small list of Redwood monitoring probe IPs to be allowed inbound to the RTP health-check endpoints.

5) Test plan before go-live
- Cross-VPC ping/traceroute, TLS handshake sample, small synthetic load (10 RPS) for 30m, KV cache warmup validation.

Can someone on your side create a temporary role/service account with minimal readonly permissions to the VPC subnet metadata (or share a sanitized inventory) so our infra team can pre-verify route overlap? If so, please email me the account name or an AWS IAM role ARN (we’ll only use it for read-only checks).

If helpful, I can paste a short checklist in the kickoff so we can mark items off live.

Ben Carter
Senior Field Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@medicohealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 08:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Medico activation runway — on-prem/VPC info & next steps

Samir — quick note on KMS/compliance items so there’s no blockers on our side:

- KMS: the ARN you provided looks good. We need to confirm key policy allows Redwood’s dedicated service principal to encrypt/decrypt (we’ll share a minimal policy snippet). If you prefer HSM/HSM-backed keys with an external HSM provider, that’s fine but we’ll need the HSM vendor cert and supported algorithms.
- Audit logs: please provide CloudTrail bucket name and retention policy or a redacted screenshot of your logging retention settings. We need evidence it persists for at least 90 days per our internal policy (enterprise customers can request longer retention).
- SOC2: once the redacted SOC2 arrives we’ll route to Security for a quick intake (should be 24–48 hours to clear).

Also: do you have any restrictions on us deploying a lightweight ingestion probe (container) for 72 hours to validate tail latency? If yes, specify the policy required for temporary deployment.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

> - KMS ARN: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01

Action items (owners & ETA):

- Kimberly: share minimal KMS policy snippet and security intake checklist (ETA: 26 Jul EOD)
- Marissa: schedule the kickoff and reserve two consecutive slots for follow-ups (ETA: 26 Jul noon PDT). Suggested: 26 Jul 20:00 UTC or 27 Jul 00:00 UTC to accommodate Samir (he’s EST).
- Vivek: prepare the deployment runbook template (network steps, probe commands, rollback) and a short-lived cert-based bastion flow for support access (ETA: 28 Jul)

- Public egress ranges not finalized — affects allowlisting for monitoring and probe IPs

Marissa — once you confirm meeting time, I’ll send an agenda with the test plan Ben pasted (ping/traceroute, TLS handshake, synthetic 10 RPS test) and request Samir’s IAM role ARN. Kimberly — please attach the KMS policy snippet in that agenda so Samir can apply it ahead of time.

Jordan
